applies_why: The judge text evaluates a D5/C5 collision involving C5's own narrowing, so it is the chain-against-chain setting the rule governs.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase never verse by verse could mean the judge must not decide or support a chain collision by isolated verse or word-count comparisons, or it could mean only that a single pressed verse need not itself state the contrary while such observations may still be noted as non-decisive support.
why: The judge's written reasons rest on chapter bounds, Matthew 1:23's application, and a word-count cutting both ways, which is verse-level weighing rather than chain-against-chain by footing.
